title: Tariffs and material prices
lines: Among the 17 building materials the brief tracks, the largest price rises from October 2025 to October 2026 were steel mill products (+32.9%), copper and brass shapes (+23.9%) and aluminum shapes (+23.3%). Fuel rose more: diesel is up 115.2%.
Prices moved less than 3% for ready-mix concrete, brick and clay tile, gypsum products (drywall), major appliances (factory price) and cement.
Tariffs of up to 50% on steel, aluminum and copper and war-driven fuel costs are both in force. The price data does not show how much of the rise is tariffs.
Raw steel made in the US: up 5.9% this year through November 14, 2026.
US sawmills: capacity fell 6.0% in a year, by a builders' association estimate for early 2026.
Single-family homes started (US): down 4.0% this year through September 2026.

Material costs apply to every new home, rental or for sale. In income-restricted rental homes the rent cannot go above a legal limit, so the part of a cost increase that rents within the limit cannot cover becomes funding gap for the building. Buyers of new for-sale homes can see it in the price.

source.text: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Producer Price Index, October 2026; production figures from the sources in the brief. Checked 2026-11-17.

note: The brief reads Bureau of Labor Statistics commodity price series, so a figure here can differ a little from the industry series shown elsewhere on this page.

brief.title: Tariffs and the cost of building homes: what rose, what did not, and whether it built anything
